rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests the critical design choice of using multimodal data (RNA + image) with a simple concatenation fusion. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines, which is foundational for the study. This is the best use of the first experiment as it isolates the impact of modality combination, a key factor in multimodal modeling.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing fusion from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best next step because it directly compares two critical multimodal design choices (fusion method) with minimal changes, helping determine if weighted fusion is beneficial without altering other factors like encoders or aggregation.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with singleprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, and resnet50 image encoder achieve ~52.6% accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to scvi_n200 RNA encoder (a more complex representation) improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether advanced encoders outperform simpler ones, aligning with principles to reduce uncertainty about critical design decisions.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder with concat fusion achieves the highest accuracy (0.536) in singleprofile settings. This experiment tests extending that promising RNA encoder to multiprofile settings while keeping image encoder and aggregation consistent, isolating the impact of profile setting. It directly builds on the best-performing configuration, efficiently exploring a key design choice with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with weighted fusion achieve high performance (0.5399 accuracy). The uncertainty is whether multiprofile settings could further improve performance. Testing config_031 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) isolates the effect of profile setting while maintaining other high-performing components, directly addressing this key design choice.

Existing evidence shows that config_031 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (a larger, more complex model) improves performance while keeping the RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion method constant. This isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and builds on the promising multiprofile/multimodal direction.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l achieve high accuracy (config_037). This experiment tests whether using transformer aggregation instead of avgpool improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It is the best use of the budget as it builds on the existing best configuration and explores a key design choice.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt (while keeping other components identical) improves performance, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of a novel encoder, addressing a key design decision with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, multiprofile, and avgpool aggregation (config_031) achieve 0.6776 accuracy. Testing config_005 (rna_only with same RNA encoder and profile settings) isolates the impact of image data. This clarifies whether multimodal benefits outweigh the complexity of adding image data, addressing a key design choice with minimal changes to the existing successful configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping other components constant) impacts performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best next step to validate if the fusion method is a critical factor, balancing exploitation of the current top-performing configuration with exploration of design choices.
